Author: WanderedWriter

Rating: General AudiencesLanguage: EnglishWords: 31,634Chapters: 5/?Kudos: 128

Summary: “The whole world will only know what Ladybug tells them. Her words will be the truth.” To the Parisian public, Ladybug wasn't a savior; she was a tyrant who abused absolute power, covered up for Hawk Moth, and allied herself with Chrysalis before being duly punished by a mysterious mystical Order. Thirty-two years later, a smuggling ring in the Gotham docks ends with a vandalized and smashed statue, from which a confused Parisian teenager emerges. Bruce knows that the young woman in his infirmary is classified as a highly dangerous threat, but when Tim discovers classified files and a school photograph reveals the face of a young Talia al Ghul, things start to get complicated. With Marinette Dupain-Cheng seemingly without memory and unsure of who to trust, Bruce will have to discover whether he's protecting a victim or harboring the monster described in the official files. Is Marinette the mastermind who orchestrated the fall of France, or simply the bug caught in something much bigger?

Summary: Five years Damian waited for the last Miraculous Ladybug manga, and the ending sucks. Enraged, he boasted he could write a better story. A mischievous, fifth-dimensional imp quickly appears and gives him a chance to prove his claim. To prevent a disappointing ending, he must change the plot as he sees fit. What would a genius detective, Robin, do in the MLB Universe, to cause Chaos of course! ​He wakes up in a world where he is dead, but Alfred is his living ally. With just seven days until the plot kicks off, Damian dedicates himself to healing the fractured Batfamily, slowly putting the pieces back together. But he can multitask. To prevent the Love Square, he decides to aggressively befriend Marinette Dupain-Cheng the only way a Wayne knows how: by replacing her friends with competent ones and burying her under a mountain of gifts. Who knew purchasing platonic affection required so much cashmere? (I am currently writing the final arc. )

Summary: New school, new chance to totally not embarrass herself; Marinette Dupain-Cheng’s plan is simple: blend in, bake macarons, and avoid drama. Instead, she lands smack between Maps (the school’s sunbeam) and Damian Wayne (the “ice prince” who could probably freeze fire).
